ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.50 to the rider's original payment method (excess distance fare); record a driver violation for the off-route segment driven without consent covering it (RD-2 / §1.3); send the driver the RD-7 notification/compliance reminder and log this notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning, first such incident). No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 11.6 km against an 8.4 km optimal route, +3.2 km, and the fare record bills 3.19 km of deviation from the billed distance against the optimal route, above the 1 km tolerance, so a refund is triggered [F1][F4][RD-1]. The whole deviation sits in one off-route segment, 12:11–12:17, which drove 4.45 km where the optimal route covers 1.58 km, adding 2.88 km and driving CLEMENTI AVENUE 4 among its roads [F3][RD-1].

The rider's consent has to be read from its words: the driver asked at 12:07 "shall I take another way?" and the rider answered at 12:08 "Can lah, but not via Clementi Avenue 4." [F7][F8]. That is a yes to a route choice made by the driver, but it is bounded: the rider expressly ruled out one road, and the consent is then a general route choice with that road excluded. The code checks the named road against the roads the segment drove; the excluded road, CLEMENTI AVENUE 4, was in fact driven, so the agreement does not reach the segment [F3][F8][RD-5]. A general yes with a road ruled out leaves that road outside the consent; the segment therefore counts under RD-2, and there is no exempt km [F8][F3][RD-5][RD-2].

The driver's assertion in his written statement that "the rider said can, so I went round" is a post-trip claim, not consent, and adds nothing beyond the chat [F10][RD-5]. RD-3 is not engaged: the rider never named a place or route the car was to go to; she named only a road to be avoided [F8][RD-3]. The traffic record is not decisive for the amount: the congestion on AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY (band 2, active 11:58–12:17) gives the segment a traffic reason, so no driver violation is recorded on that ground, but under RD-2 the amount still turns only on whether the rider agreed to or asked for this route, and she did not [F11][F3][RD-4][RD-2][RD-5].

Amount, from the trace's arithmetic and the numbers on record: (3.19 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4096/km = $4.50, which matches the excess distance item billed for 3.19 km at this trip's distance fare [$F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; there is no surge on this trip [F4][F5][F6][FARE-0][RD-2]. The outcome is refund_partial $4.50, consistent as well with the fare-dispute and route-deviation precedents of the same shape (DISP-2026-0089, DISP-2026-0142) [PREC-1]. RD-6 does not apply: the driver's one upheld dispute in 90 days is not a route deviation (route: 0), so no account flag [F17][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's message [F8] at 12:08 — before the segment began at 12:11 — answers the driver's 12:07 proposal [F7] with a general yes ('Can lah') but expressly rules out Clementi Avenue 4. Her words name only a road to be avoided, so this is general route consent with an excluded road, not agreement to a named road; the segment drove CLEMENTI AVENUE 4 [F3], so the consent does not cover it and the segment counts under RD-2 / RD-5 (§1.2–1.3). No traffic reason can exempt it, since RD-2 turns only on consent [F11][RD-4][RD-2].

element_findings.reason: The rider message sent before the segment [F8] agrees to a driver route choice but expressly excludes Clementi Avenue 4, and that road was driven on the segment [F3]; the agreement therefore does not cover the segment, so it counts under RD-2 / RD-5 (§1.2).
No rider message before the segment named a place or route the car was to go to; the only road named [F8] is one to be avoided, so RD-3 gives no exemption.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver did give notice of the reroute before the deviation: his 12:07 message [F7] precedes the segment start at 12:11 [F3], so the rider was not left uninformed and the RD-7 reminder/log step is not triggered by an uninformed reroute. The refund here follows from the consent's scope under RD-2/RD-5, not from a notice failure [F7][F8][RD-5].

The part of C8 asking for a driver violation on the ground that the reroute had no traffic justification is rejected: RD-4 is satisfied here, the AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY on the replaced stretch was at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) from 11:58–12:17, active before and during the segment [F11][F3], so no violation is recorded on that ground; the excess distance fare is refunded because the rider's consent excluded a road that was driven [F8][F3][RD-5][RD-2].

The claim that the traffic reason removes the refund is rejected: RD-4 only settles whether a driver violation is recorded, while under RD-2 the amount turns on whether the rider agreed to or asked for the route, and her consent excluded Clementi Avenue 4, which the segment drove [F11][F8][F3][RD-4][RD-2][RD-5].

The claim that the exchange was a purely general route choice is rejected as to scope: the rider ruled out a road ('but not via Clementi Avenue 4' [F8]) and that road appears in the segment's roads driven [F3], so the consent does not cover the segment [RD-5][RD-2].

The claim that only a portion of the excess distance fare attributable to the excluded road should be refunded, or none at all, is rejected: no record ties a part of the segment to the excluded road and a part to consented roads, so the whole segment counts and the full excess distance fare of $4.50 is refundable under RD-2 [F3][F4][RD-2][RD-5].
The statement that RD-6 flagging does not apply is correct and is not a rejected claim as to outcome; the record shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F17], so no flag_account is entered [RD-6].

The rider's safety screen finding is correct on the material read: the chat and complaint contain a route carve-out and a fare objection only, with no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8], so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not triggered.
